answer: To resist sybil attacks, an AI-agent economy can demand that every new identity register by solving a unique computational puzzle whose solution is recorded as a pearl on a shared atlas of trusted agents. Generating each pearl requires significant GPU time and energy, so an attacker who tries to spin up thousands of fake identities must pay a steep, non-amortizable cost in electricity and hardware for every sonnet of bogus accounts they compose. This makes mass fake-identity creation economically irrational while legitimate agents pay the cost only once.
